topics.name: Modals: would like, have to, must, should, might

questions.prompt: Pick the sentence with the correct collective noun.
options: A fleet of bees flew past the window.
A bunch of bees flew past the window.
A swarm of bees flew past the window.
questions.rule: We say a swarm of bees. A fleet is for ships and a bunch is for grapes, keys or flowers.

options: What a beautiful view of the earth!
What an beautiful view of the earth!
How a beautiful view of the earth!
questions.rule: An exclamation can start with What a + adjective + noun: What a beautiful view! It ends with !

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.

options: packing
packs
packed

questions.rule: Past perfect = had + past participle: had already packed.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.

options: follow
following
followed

questions.rule: After a modal like must, use the base verb: must follow.

options: flock
swarm
herd
questions.rule: We say a herd of cattle, a flock of sheep and a swarm of bees.

questions.after: like to visit the moon one day.
options: will
would
am
questions.rule: would like to is the polite way to say what you want: I would like to visit ...
Reported speech: said that + subject + past verb: She said that she was tired.

chat: Can we go outside the dome without space suits?
options: No, we have to wear space suits outside.
No, we has to wear space suits outside.
No, we have to wearing space suits outside.
questions.rule: have to + base verb shows a rule: we have to wear. Use has to only with he/she/it.

chat: What did you see at the circus?
options: We saw a team of gymnast doing high jumps.
We saw a teams of gymnasts doing high jumps.
We saw a team of gymnasts doing high jumps.
questions.rule: a team of + plural noun: a team of gymnasts. A cannot go with teams.

options: Sayali said that she was excited.
Sayali said that I was excited.
Sayali said that she were excited.
questions.rule: I becomes she, and am moves back to was: Sayali said that she was excited.

questions.prompt: Pick the sentence with the correct tense.
options: The shuttle had landed before the sun rose.
The shuttle had land before the sun rose.
The shuttle has landed before the sun rose.
questions.rule: The earlier of two past actions takes had + past participle: had landed before the sun rose.

options: You should listens to the receptionist.
You should listen to the receptionist.
You should to listen to the receptionist.
questions.rule: After should use the base verb with no to: should listen.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.

options: flock's
flocks
flocking

questions.rule: Collective nouns have plurals too: three flocks of sheep, just like herds and teams.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.

options: his
himself
he

questions.rule: The subject of was needs the subject pronoun he, not him: Ravi said that he was very hungry.

questions.before: When Sayali opened her tiffin box, her little brother
options: has
have
had
questions.rule: The brother ate first, before Sayali opened the box, so use the past perfect: had already eaten.

questions.after: not buy anything from unauthorised shops.
options: should
has
have
questions.rule: should not + base verb gives advice: You should not buy ... has/have not buy is wrong.
have to + base verb shows something necessary: We have to carry ...

chat: Why didn't you call me from the moon?
options: Sorry, I had forget my phone at the base.
Sorry, I had forgotten my phone at the base.
Sorry, I have forgotten my phone at the base yesterday.
questions.rule: Past perfect = had + past participle: had forgotten. Yesterday never goes with have forgotten.

questions.source: The teacher said, "Sayali is a good student."
options: The teacher said that Sayali is being a good student.
The teacher said that Sayali was a good student.
The teacher told that Sayali was a good student.
questions.rule: After said, is moves back to was. Told needs a person after it (told us).

questions.prompt: Change the subject into the plural.
options: The teams are practising.
The teams is practising.
The team are practisings.
questions.rule: The plural of team is teams, and a plural subject takes are: The teams are practising.

options: How bright the stars are!
How bright the stars is!
What bright the stars are!
questions.rule: How + adjective + subject + verb!: How bright the stars are! Plural stars takes are.

questions.prompt: Pick the sentence with the correct tense.
options: By the time the bell rang, we had finished the test.
By the time the bell rang, we have finished the test.
By the time the bell rang, we had finish the test.
questions.rule: By the time + past: the earlier action takes had + past participle: had finished.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.

options: fallen
falling
fall

questions.rule: After might use the base verb: might fall.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.

options: had
has
having

questions.rule: After told (past), the earlier action moves to the past perfect: she had bought earrings the day before.

questions.after: of grapes lay on the table.
options: herd
fleet
bunch
questions.rule: We say a bunch of grapes, a herd of cattle and a fleet of ships.
An interjection like Oh dear, starts the sentence, and the exclamation ends with !
had never + past participle: had never seen. such comes before the adjective + noun.

options: She said that the shops outside was not safe.
She said that the shops outside were not safe.
She said to that the shops outside were not safe.
questions.rule: The shops is plural, so were. Write said that, not said to that.

options: Yes, please. I would loves some.
Yes, please. I would to love some.
Yes, please. I would love some.
questions.rule: After would use the base verb with no to: I would love some.

questions.source: The shuttle landed. Then the door was opened.
options: The door was opened after the shuttle has landed.
The door was opened after the shuttle had landed.
The door had opened after the shuttle was landed.
questions.rule: The earlier action (landing) takes the past perfect: after the shuttle had landed.

options: A army of ants marched across the floor.
An army of ant marched across the floor.
An army of ants marched across the floor.
questions.rule: army starts with a vowel sound, so an army; it is followed by the plural ants.

options: Neha said that her grandmother live in Kolkata.
Neha said that her grandmother lived in Kolkata.
Neha said that she grandmother lived in Kolkata.
questions.rule: After said the verb moves to the past: lived. Before a noun use the possessive her.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.

options: having
had
was

questions.rule: She lost the pen before she felt sad, so use the past perfect: had lost. She have is never correct.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.

options: running
runs
run

questions.rule: had to + base verb: had to run. The past is shown by had, not by the main verb.

options: were
be
was
questions.rule: After said use the past, and he takes was: he was tired.

questions.after: of birds visit our lake in winter.
options: flock
flocks
flock's
questions.rule: Many needs a plural noun: many flocks of birds.
must not + base verb tells us something is not allowed: must not run.

chat: Did you watch the circus on Sunday?
options: No, it had ended before we got there.
No, it has ended before we got there.
No, it had end before we got there.
questions.rule: The circus ended first, so use had ended before the simple past got there.

questions.source: Sayali said, "I am buying earrings for my mother."
options: Sayali said that she was buying earrings for her mother.
Sayali said that she was buying earrings for my mother.
Sayali said that she was buy earrings for her mother.
questions.rule: I and my become she and her; am buying becomes was buying.

questions.source: We have to pay for the tour.
options: We do not has to pay for the tour.
We does not have to pay for the tour.
We do not have to pay for the tour.
questions.rule: have to makes its negative with do not: We do not have to pay.

questions.prompt: Pick the sentence with the correct tenses.
options: Sayali realise her mistake only after her mother had held the earrings.
Sayali realised her mistake only after her mother had held the earrings.
Sayali realised her mistake only after her mother had hold the earrings.
questions.rule: The main action is simple past realised; the earlier one is had + past participle: had held.

options: They went on a three-day trip to the moon.
They went on a three-days trip to the moon.
They went on an three-day trip to the moon.
questions.rule: A hyphenated number + noun before a noun stays singular: a three-day trip, not three-days.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.

options: have
having
had

questions.rule: After told (past), an earlier past action takes the past perfect: had landed.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.

options: wolfs
wolves
wolf's

questions.rule: a pack of + plural noun. The plural of wolf is wolves (f changes to ves).

questions.before: If you go outside without a space suit, you
options: might
ought
have
questions.rule: might + base verb shows a possibility: you might get hurt. ought and have need to.
Reported speech: said that + subject + past verb: the earrings were too heavy.

chat: What did your mother say about the trip?
options: She said that it was too expensive but I should go.
She said that it were too expensive but I should go.
She said me that it was too expensive but I should go.
questions.rule: It takes was. Said is not followed by a person: say said that or told me that.

chat: What did you see in the sky from the moon?
options: I saw a galaxy of star and a shining earth.
I saw an galaxy of stars and a shining earth.
I saw a galaxy of stars and a shining earth.
questions.rule: a galaxy of + plural noun: a galaxy of stars. galaxy starts with a consonant sound, so a.

options: What a beautiful view it is!
How a beautiful view it is!
What a beautiful view is it!
questions.rule: What a + adjective + noun + subject + verb!: What a beautiful view it is! (not is it).

questions.source: Sayali paid for the earrings. Then she ran to her friends.
options: Sayali paid for the earrings before she had ran to her friends.
Sayali had paid for the earrings before she ran to her friends.
Sayali had pay for the earrings before she ran to her friends.
questions.rule: The first action (paying) takes had paid; the later one stays in the simple past: ran.
